correctness.rationale: C: For normal N spectral theorem proves bounded-orbit subspace E([0,r])H under scaled modulus, bounded-orbit limit is its atom at r; SAE requires spectral gap strictly below r. The left-gap set J_K handles spectral accumulation correctly. For compact metrizable K, Cantor–Bendixson perfect kernel P and isolated points I satisfy closure(P∪I)=K. Construct a nonatomic finite measure with full support P and weighted atoms precisely at countable A, obtain L²(K,µ) separable and M_t positive/invertible with K support and atom set A. Converse: separability gives at most countably many mutually orthogonal positive-eigenvalue projections and isolated spectral points have nonzero projections. Tested boundary cases singleton, purely perfect/Cantor, isolated endpoints, and nonempty atoms. Optional packaged finite Cantor checks were read but not treated as an infinite proof.
residual_risks: Positive self-adjoint T on separable complex H; nonempty compact K subset [1,2], countable A containing isolated points; zero scalar trivially satisfies all three.
